## What changed

Two candidates were generated for this task and **both were rejected**; the champion at the end
of the run is still the seed. So the answer to "what changed" is: nothing shipped. But the two
attempts are the only real optimizer signal v1 produced, and they are worth reading as
experiments rather than as failures.

**`cand_0001` — "Force config-hierarchy trace even when job logs are missing."** Four edits to
`SKILL.md`, all additive:

- a new **"Investigation Contract (non-negotiable)"** section with three rules — echo the user's
  IDs verbatim; call `query_aap2` + `lookup_catalog_item` + `fetch_github_file` +
  `search_github_repo` at least once each; name the catalog item and `scm_ref` in the report;
- a rewritten Tips bullet keeping `get_job_log`-first behaviour but adding a mandatory
  `find_jobs(status=failed)` fallback on `east`+`west` when every supplied ID returns *not found*
  on every controller;
- a new **"Fallback: When Specific Job Data Is Unavailable"** section spelling out a 4-step flow;
- a tightened "MANDATORY `fetch_github_file`" preamble closing the loophole the agent used to skip
  the config trace on a *not found*.

Rule 2 was aimed squarely at this task's `trajectory: 0.000`. The journal's stated expectation was
explicit and quantified: *"trajectory 0 → 1 on 26/30 completed trials, +0.5 per trial to reward."*

**`cand_0002` — "Redirect 'not found on all controllers' from an ask-user dead-end to a compact
Fallback pivot."** It dropped the Investigation Contract entirely — the optimizer's own reading of
`cand_0001`'s failure was that a second layer of rules is ignored — and kept only the pivot,
guarded to fire exclusively when every user-supplied ID returns *not found* on every valid
controller.

Both were evaluated on 30 trials on `val` and both scored below the seed: **paired Δ̄ −0.092** and
**−0.160**, rejected at `gate_k_se = 1.0`. Neither is recorded as fixing or breaking a *named*
task — the run's `rejected.jsonl` shows `fixed={—} broke={—}` for both, because the val split is
only two tasks and neither crossed a pass/fail boundary.

## What worked

**One thing worked, exactly twice, and it is the most interesting number in the whole v1
experiment.**

Every trial of the seed on this task scored either `0.333` or `0.000` — no other value appears in
30 seed trials, 30 `seed_train` trials, or 30 `FINAL` trials. `0.333` decomposes as
`0.5 × trajectory 0.000 + 0.5 × assertions 0.667`: the seed reliably recovered **4 of this task's
6 `answer_contains` strings** and *never once* matched the 13-call trajectory. That is a ceiling,
not a distribution.

`cand_0002` broke it. One of its 30 trials scored **0.833** — which decomposes as
`0.5 × trajectory 1.000 + 0.5 × assertions 0.667`. **A full trajectory match.** It is the only
trajectory match ever recorded on this task by any artifact in any v1 run, and `cand_0002` also
produced the only one on `-0048` (a `0.900`, same run). Two matches in 60 candidate trials.

The journal had predicted the number before it happened: *"Achievable upper bound on 0047 stays
~0.83 while these persist."* The one trial that got there hit **0.8333**.

So the rejected candidate did something the champion cannot do. It just did it about 3% of the
time, while making the ordinary case markedly worse.

## What didn't

**The mean, decisively, for both candidates.** Read the per-trial vectors in
`results/v1/per_task_scores.json` rather than the means:

| artifact | trials at `0.333`+ | trials at `0.000` | best single trial |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| `seed` (22 valid) | 19 | 3 | 0.333 |
| `cand_0001` | 20 | 10 | 0.333 |
| `cand_0002` | 11 | 19 | **0.833** |

`cand_0001` did not lift trajectory on a single trial out of 30 — the Investigation Contract's
Rule 2 produced no trajectory credit at all — and it converted three additional trials to outright
zero. `cand_0002` traded nineteen zeros for one 0.833. Both are correctly rejected by a
mean-based paired gate. Neither is a "regression" in the sense of damage shipped: the champion
never moved.

**The optimizer's own diagnosis of why is on the record and is the useful part.** From the
journal's refuted-hypotheses section: *"The reader (sonnet-4-5) does not obey a second set of rules
layered on top of an already-detailed skill — the fix has to be a MODIFICATION of the existing
decision points, not an addition."* And separately, that *"echo every user-supplied identifier
verbatim"* is **not** the missing behaviour. Two hypotheses were tested and both were falsified,
which is more than most iterations of anything produce.

**And eight of thirty seed trials never ran.** The `seed` vector has `null` at eight consecutive
positions (trials 16–23), all `NetworkConnectionError`. That is not eight independent samples of
bad luck — it is one outage window, and the identical eight positions are missing from `-0048`'s
seed vector in the same run. The journal called this out at the time as *"Network/harness errors
(t16-t23 subset) — ~5/30 trials"*; the rollouts on disk say **8**, so the run under-counted its own
infrastructure loss by three trials. The candidates, evaluated later, lost none.

That last point matters for the headline: the seed's `val` figure is **0.288 with those eight
dropped** and **0.211 with them counted as zero**. Both appear in the ledger. cap-evolve reported
the first.

## What we can (or can't) learn

**We can learn that the trajectory half of this task's reward is reachable but not reliably
reachable, and that this was discovered by a candidate the gate threw away.** A single 0.833
against a seed that is pinned at 0.333 is weak evidence — one trial — but it is *positive*
evidence about the ceiling, and it is exactly the kind of finding a mean-based accept/reject
decision is designed to discard. The gate made the right call for the champion and the wrong call
for the knowledge: `cand_0002` should have been re-run at higher `n` on 0047 alone rather than
dropped.

**We cannot learn much about the skill from the baseline row, and this task is the reason we know
why.** Its contract demands 13 calls under a `subset` match, one of which is
`lookup_catalog_item` — a tool the babylon simulator serves, and babylon was **not running** when
the 30-task sweep scored this task on 2026-08-12. Under a `subset` match one uncallable op fails the
whole containment, so the `trajectory: 0.000` in the baseline row was guaranteed before the agent
started. 25 of the 30 v1 tasks are in that position; see `results/v1/summary.md`.

**But this task is also one of only two places in the branch where that gap is demonstrably
closed.** `cand_0002` scored a full `trajectory: 1.000` here on 2026-08-14, which is only possible if
`lookup_catalog_item` was callable by then — and the same candidate did it on
[`-0048`](v1-aap2-0048.md), the other task that demands it. So the tool surface changed between
2026-08-12 and 2026-08-14, and **no file in this branch or in the source worktree records when or by
whom.** The practical consequence: this task's baseline `0.000` and its pilot numbers were measured
against different harnesses, and the 28 baseline-only rows elsewhere in v1 were all measured against
the earlier, narrower one. Do not line them up in a single column.

What is left of the reward-level reading is the assertion half, which was reachable throughout — and
it never moved. Every non-zero trial of every artifact on this task, in every one of the four v1 runs,
scored assertions `0.667` and no other value: **4 of 6 strings, never 3, never 5**. That is a hard
ceiling on the half of the reward the harness was not interfering with, and no candidate touched it.
The demanded-length story (13 calls is long) is a secondary and confounded effect — see the
`op_count_confound_note` in `results.json`.

**We cannot treat the `test` number as a result at all.** The pilot ran with
`train == val == test == {0047, 0048}` and cap-evolve emitted its own warning:
`"test overlaps train/val (no-holdout fit) — the test number is NOT held out; report it as a fit
metric"`. The `0.278` in the table above is a re-measurement of the same two tasks the optimizer
was tuned on. `test_delta` is `+0.0` because the champion is the seed.

**The concrete next step this task argues for** is not a better skill edit. It is: fix the
contract (13 mechanically-scraped calls is not a specification of correct behaviour), fix the
infrastructure (an 8-trial outage inside a 30-trial measurement), and only then re-run — with
`cand_0002`'s pivot as the first candidate to retry, since it is the only edit with any
demonstrated upside on this task.
